front.title: Cross-Handle Compute Lease: Identity-Addressed Bounded Execution Over an Agent-Frame Substrate

abstract.t: This memo specifies a Cross-Handle Compute Lease: a bounded, revocable, turn-metered primitive by which one identity-bound principal, addressed by a ~handle, asks for a defined task to run on the machine of a different principal, also addressed by a ~handle, over an existing agent-frame substrate. The lease moves general computation between identities without opening an inbound network path on the host's machine and without exposing a network endpoint to the borrower; the address is the identity and the transport is the identity-event stream. The memo specifies four frame kinds for the lease lifecycle, a four-rung trust ladder under which one envelope serves intra-organisational, cross-organisational, datacentre and open-market deployments, an isolation requirement that holds at every rung, an identity-inference exclusion invariant that prevents the leased computation from performing inference about the host, and a turn-metered settlement model in which the lease value passes between the two parties unsplit and the protocol operator holds no other party's funds. Sessions between machines held by the same ~handle are outside the memo's scope.
